data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The large service is strictly more resilient because its internal redundancy can be made formally independent, whereas the independence of decentralized nodes is at best empirically correlated and thus vulnerable to unknown common causes; empirical uncorrelation does not imply structural independence.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The formal verification of the large service's isolation domains is incomplete or contains errors.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The decentralized network employs a mechanism that provides structural guarantees equivalent to formal verification (e.g., cryptographic proofs of disjointness).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The threat model used for formal verification does not capture the relevant class of shared causes.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Formal verification of isolation domains (using diverse OS kernels, compilers, and hardware) provides a mathematical guarantee of independence against a specified threat model. Decentralized nodes, lacking a central designer, can only exhibit observed uncorrelation, which provides no guarantee against novel or unobserved shared causes. In resilience engineering, guarantees dominate observations.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
